title: Pediatrics
description: Paediatrics — milestones, infectious diseases, vaccination and organ systems.

questions.stem: An infant presents to Well Baby Clinic. She can keep her head up unsupported and need back support to set. She can smile and can reach mouth. What is the developmental age in months?

A 2-week-old infant seen in the clinic. Rubbing side of his mouth with tip of the little finger is one of the primitive reflexes (see image). What is expected age (in months) for this reflex to disappear?
A 2-week-old infant seen in screening clinic (see image). What is expected age (in months) for this reflex to disappear?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother. She is concerned of bed-wetting overnight despite toilet training, compared to his sister when she was in his age she controls herself. Until what age this is considered as a normal behaviour?
When assessing development in a 9-month-old infant, which of the following is expected to observe at this age?

options.text: Beginning to use a spoon rather sloppily

questions.stem: A 7-month-old infant visits Well Baby Clinic. Which of the following this infant should be able to do?

options.text: Hold crayon and draw a circle
Transfer objects from one hand to the other
Use thumb and index finger in crude pincer grasp

questions.stem: A 15-month-old child brought to the clinic by his parents. He was born at 36 weeks by normal vaginal delivery. At 8 months' test for hearing was done, which was normal. The parents say that he babbles, but does not speak 2-3 word phrases yet. On physical examination, the child appears normal. Which of the following is the appropriate action?

options.text: Reassure the parents that this is a normal variant

questions.stem: A child who can jump on 2 feet, build a tower of 6 blocks, use 2 word phrases and compares 2 items. What is the developmental age?

A 4-year-old boy present to the clinic with a worried mother, for general assessment and evaluation of his development. He can hop on 1 foot but not able to balance for 10 seconds, draw square, tells a story but not able to use the future tens and has a preferred friend. Which of the following is the most appropriate response to his mother?

options.text: He is growing normally according to his age
He has delayed development in gross and fine motor aspect
He is growing normally but delayed in the speech and language
He is delayed in all aspect and required further investigation

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child presented to the clinic with delayed language and speech, and learning difficulties. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?
The illnesses and problems children encounter are highly age dependent. Which of the following represent an infant age group?
Which of the following phases contribute the most for the final height of the child?
Which of the following statements is normal weight gain in infants?

options.text: Double their birth weight at 10 months
Mean weight gain by 10 g/day in the first 3 months
Mean weight gain by 15 g/day in the first 3 months
Mean weight gain by 30 g/day in the first 3 months

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate advice to a mother about the breastfeeding schedule for her full-term newborn in the first year?

options.text: On demand every 2-4 hr for first 2 months
On demand 6 times per day for first 2 months
On demand 6-8 times per day at age 8-12 months

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common reaction to a parent's illness in 12-year old girl considering her developmental stage?

options.text: Difficulty speaking directly about strong or difficult feelings
Unable to understand or appreciate details of diagnosis, prognosis and treatment
Incorporate themes of illness in their play, such as pretending to have their parent's symptoms
Likely to shift to earlier, less mature behaviors (e.g., fussiness, difficulty with separations or bedtime

questions.stem: An 8-week-old infant presents by his mother to Well-Baby Clinic worried about her baby crying with diagnosis of infantile colic. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling should be given?

options.text: Infants cry an average of 5 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually decreasing
Infants cry an average of 6 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually increasing
Infants cry an average of 2 hours per day, peaking at 6 month of age and gradually decreasing
Infants cry an average of 2.2 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually decreasing

questions.stem: An infant sits in the tripod position, can roll from prone to supine and vice versa and attempts to reach a toy beyond reach but cannot pick up cereals between 2 fingers. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A mother of a 3-year-old child asks about his language development. He easily communicates with other children and 75% of his speech is understood by strangers. He asks questions frequently and follows 2-part commands. What is the best description of this language development?

In a prone position, an infant can lift his head 45 off the examination table and moves his head from side to side while following an object. He smiles and coos when the doctor plays with him, but cannot maintain a seated poison. What is the age in months this child most likely at
Which of the following language milestones is appropriate for a 4-year-old child?

options.text: Can count to 4 and tell a story

questions.stem: By what age in months should a child smile?

A child is brought for a well-child visit. He is healthy and developing normally. The child can name 4 colours, define 5 words, understand prepositions, hops on 1 foot, and gets dressed with little assistance. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A 6-month-old child is brought to the paediatrician for a well-child visit. The infant was born at full term after a normal pregnancy and spontaneous vaginal delivery. The linear growth and the amount of weight gained over the past 6 months are both appropriate. The mother began feeding the infant pureed baby foods approximately 1 month before while also continuing breastfeeding. The infant has been well since birth. The physical examination is normal for age. developmental screening exam is performed. Which of the following gross motor skills is most appropriate at his age?

options.text: Rolls from prone to supine position
Rolls from supine to prone position

questions.stem: By what age in months should a child learn to speak a few words?

A child is brought for a health maintenance check. The parent states that the child sits up alone without support, pulls himself into a standing position, explores around furniture, crawls without difficulty. grasps objects with a thumb and forefinger, uses repetitive consonants such as "dada", and responds to the sound of his own name. What age in months is the child most probably at?

A 4-month-old girl is brought to the Paediatric Clinic for a routine monthly exam. The baby smiles back at people and imitates facial expressions. She uses eyes and hands together and reaches out with one hand for a toy. There is babbling along with a facial expression. The girl pushes up to her elbows when lying on the tummy. Weight 7300 grams (=50th percentile) Length 67 cm (=75th percentile) Which additional developmental milestone is most likely to have?
Which of the following is usually the first sign of puberty in boys?

An apparently normal child is being evaluated. He runs around, tells short stories and plays a "father role". He draws his brother with a head, hands and feet. He undresses himself for the examination. What is the most likely age of this child?
Which of the following is the most typical milestone for a 4-year-old child?

A 5-month-old baby referred to the doctor from the Well-Baby Clinic. His mother is concerned, because he could not pass the developmental screening tests done by the nurse. What is the best developmental test would help the doctor to reassure the mother?
Which of the following can the average 3-year-old child perform?

options.text: With alternating feet catch a ball

questions.stem: While in the clinic, a child runs towards the doctor, walks upstairs with one hand held and pours out pellets from a bo]le. The child does not handle a spoon well and cannot put 3 words together. What is the approximate age in months?
During a health supervision examination, a mother reports that her son can say his name, feeds himself, separates easily from parents and rides a tricycle. What is the developmental age in years?

While at the clinic, an infant crawl toward the doctor, rolls over, sits briefly, transfers objects from hand to hand and grasps objects using his radial palm. The infant is unable to use a pincer grasp. What is the approximate age in months?

A child walks with one hand held, says a few words besides "mama" and "dada", and picks up pellets with an unassisted pincer grasp, but does not insert them into a bo]le. What is the approximate age in months?

While in the dinic, a child demonstrates an ability to run, is able to open a door and climb onto furniture. The child uses 3-word sentences, but does not know his full name and does not climb up stairs using alternate feet. Which of the following is the approximate age in years?

An infant lies with his head to one side and raises his head slightly, but the head lags when pulling up to a sieng position. The infant smiles when involved in social interactions and follows moving objects 180 degrees, but does not a]empi to reach for them. What is the approximate developmental age in weeks?

A child's developmental assessment conforms the following (see table). Motor Walks alone, crawls up stairs Adaptive Makes a tower of three cubes, makes a line with crayons Language Jargon, follows simple commands Social Indicates desire by pointing Which of the following is the most likely age in months?
Which of the following is a developmental screening tool that relies only on information from the parents?

options.text: Safety word inventory and literacy screener

questions.stem: When a mother placed her infant on the examining table, the infant laughs out loudly. As the doctor approaches him, he squeals and reaches for his mother. What is the most likely developmental month for this child?

A child accompanied by his parents walked into the examination room. He is holding a ball. The doctor asks to let him see the ball; he threw the ball towards the doctor. Then he reaches out to catch it when the doctor throws the ball back to him. He draws a straight line on the paper and then picks up a few blocks from the floor and stacks one on the top of the other. What is the most likely developmental month for this child?

A child enters the clinic and says "hi" to the doctor then turns to the mother and says "milk". The mother gives her a bottle of milk, and the child tries to give her doll a drink. The mother shakes her head, and the child says "no". After which the child smiles and points to her own mouth and says "mouth". When her mother wipes the doll's face, the child says "me" and begins to imitate the mother's action and gives the doll a hug. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A 9-year-old boy is brought for a check-up. Parents are worried because he is short. On examination, his height is below the 5th percentile for his age but increasing steadily. The parents ask if he will always be short in the future. What is the most important factor to answer the question?

During a routine check-up, a child shakes hands, knows his name, gender and age. He can dress with help and ride a tricycle. He points to red colours when asked to do so but had difficulty copying a square. What is the age in years this child is most likely at?

A 13-year-old boy comes to the clinic complaining of fatigue, non-productive cough, low-grade fever and night sweats over the past 7 weeks. He also mentioned that he has had 2 episodes of hemoptysis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents with a high-grade fever, malaise, conjunctivitis, coryza, and a cough. A rash of discrete pink macules recently began on the face and extends to the hands and feet. The child also had small, whitish spots inside the mouth before the rash appeared. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child presents to Emergency Department with fever, poor feeding and vomiting for 3 days after a flu-like illness. On examination, she looks sick, lethargic and capillary refill is 4 seconds. Cardiopulmonary monitor attached and intravenous access attained. Blood pressure 62/46 mmH Heart rate 156 /min Respiratory rate 48 /min Temperature 38.2 °C Oxygen saturation 92% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most common cause of shock in children?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic for his yearly physical examination. His history revealed various behavioral issues, including poor interaction with peers and family, delayed language development, repetitive movements, and difficulty accepting change. The child stiffens physically when touched, does not respond to the examiner, and does not make eye contact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother. She noticed that the child has been eating clay and paper for the last 4 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

A 9-year-old boy brought to the clinic by his mother. She is concered of bed-wetting overnight for one month. He was dry since age of 6 years and the mother gave history of fever and foul smell of his urine recently. Urine dipstick done (see lab result). Blood pressure 90/60 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.6 °C Color dark yellow clear or light yellow Appearance cloudy clear Specific gravity 1030 1001-1030 Nitrite present Absent Leukocytes 7 0-3 per high power field Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old child presents to the Paediatric Outpatient Clinic with a 2-day history of constipation lethargy, and fever. The child was born to a 25 year-old primigravida and is being breached. On examination, the child has flatened facies, an inability to smile or gaze away when a light is shined directly in the eye. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 140 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Temperature 38.2° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with a 2-day history of vomiting and diarrhoea. The stool is watery without mucus or blood. Examination reveals that the infant is only mildly dehydrated. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 4-year-old girl is brought to the clinic for prolonged diarrhoea. On examination, she looks pale. She is drinking 3 pints of goat's milk/day, and a very fussy eater (see lab results). Hb 59 112-165 g/L MCV 102 80-95 f1 MCHC 390 260-340 g/L Which of the following is the most significant in the past medical history?

A previously healthy 4-month-old uncircumcised boy is brought to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of fever. He has not had vomiting, diarrhea, cough, or nasal congestion. There has been no known contact with ill persons. He has continued to breastfeed and has not had a decrease in the number of wet diapers. He is mildly ill-appearing but alert and interactive. Examination shows no focus of infection. Urinary catheterization is performed (see lab results). - Temperature 39.1 °C ● pH: 7.5 (4.3-8) ● Specific gravity: 1010 (1001-1030) ● Protein: Absent (Absent) ● Glucose: Absent (Absent) ● Ketones: Absent (Absent) ● Nitrite: Positive (Absent) ● Leukocytes: 30-40 (0-3 per high power field) ● Erythrocytes: 5-10 (0-2 per high power field) Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical therapy?

A 4-month-old girl with unilateral purulent effusion, decreased tympanic membrane mobility with pneumatic otoscopy, no fever, and no other symptoms. She is breastfeeding very well and does not use a pacifier. She has no recent history of infections. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options.text: ENT referral for evaluation of tympanostomy tubes

questions.stem: A 19-month-old boy presented to the clinic with right lower eyelid swelling, erythema, and tenderness for 1 day. He has a fever reaching up to 38.5 °C with decreased appetite and activity. He was given diphenhydramine without any improvement of the eyelid swelling. His parent denied any visual disturbances, diplopia, or any other swelling. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl is complaining of a sore throat for the last 2 days. Today, she has developed a fever of 38.7 °C when measured at home, which has been relieved by acetaminophen. On examination, she was found to have tender anterior cervical adenopathy and pharyngeal and tonsillar exudate. The rest of her physical exam is unremarkable. Which of the following is the best next step toward diagnosis?

options.text: Fine needle aspiration for cervical adenopathy

questions.stem: A 4-year-old girl presented to the clinic with a history of fever for the last 3 days associated with sore throat and decreased oral intake. She also has difficulty in swallowing solid food. On examination, she has a palpable cervical lymph node that is about 2 cm in size. Which of the following is the most important step in evaluation?

options.text: Fine needle aspiration of the lymph node

questions.stem: A 4-year-old girl presented to the clinic with a history of fever for the last 3 days associated with sore throat and decreased oral intake. She also has difficulty in swallowing solid food. Her vaccination is up to date. On examination, she has a palpable cervical lymph node that is about 2 cm in size, tender and fluctuates. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 5-year-old boy is diagnosed with group A streptococcus tonsillitis and started on antibiotic treatment. He has a 2-year-old brother who is well and asymptomatic. Which of the following is the best approach for his brother?

options.text: Throat swab for rapid antigen detection test

questions.stem: A newborn baby boy is born to an unbooked 25-year-old mother. The mother has developed febrile illness immediately after birth but she is otherwise stable. She does not have a record for any of the transmissible infections. She asked if she can breastfeed her baby. In which of the following conditions is breastfeeding or expressed breast milk in the immediate postpartum period acceptable?

options.text: Expressed breast milk of HIV mother
Expressed breast milk of untreated active tuberculosis

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child seen in the clinic with fever and sore throat. She has had contact with child developed flu-like symptoms. Throat exam showed mild hyperaemia. Rapid throat test was negative for streptococcal infection and throat swab sent for culture. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the best management at this stage?

options.text: Start amoxicillin for 10 days regardless of culture result

questions.stem: A 9-month-old infant presents with a history of fever, irritability and right ear rubbing. Ear exam showed air-fluid levels and bulging tympanic membrane. Blood pressure 70/50 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following organisms is the most causative agent in paediatrics acute otitis media?
A 3-year-old child presented to the clinic with a skin lesion that is not itchy. No history of fever and no previous illness (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following intervals (in days) defines fever of unknown origin in paediatrics?

A 7-year-old girl presents with fever, abdominal pain and vomiting. On examination, she looks unwell with suprapubic tenderness, but no rebound tenderness nor guarding. Bed side dipstick done (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 39 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result / Normal Values Color turbid / clear or light yellow Appearance cloudy / clear Nitrite pesent / Absent Leukocytes 22 / 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 3 / 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 3-year-old child presented with fever, headache, difficulty swallowing and throat pain. On examination, there is intense inflammation of the tonsils with purulent exudate that is more membranous in appearance. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 150 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Oxygen saturation 96 % Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 7-month-old baby presented to the clinic with a history of fever, irritability and disturbed sleeping for 2 days. Ear examination showed perforation of the eardrum with pus visible in the external canal. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 115 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Oxygen saturation 97 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old baby presented to the clinic with history of fever, irritability and disturb sleeping for 2 days. Ear examination showed perforation of the eardrum with pus visible in the external canal. Blood pressure 110/70 mmg Heart rate 115 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 39 °C Oxygen saturation 97 % Which of the following is the most common causative organism?

A 4-year-old boy previously healthy came to the clinic with a history of limping for the last 2 days. On physical examination, he is keeping his left leg flexed and refusing to move it or allowing anyone to touch it. Imaging is showing effusion of the left hip. Blood pressure 90/61 mmH Heart rate 126 /min Respiratory rate 29 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Oxygen saturation 98 % Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 4-year-old child presented with itchy and scratching skin lesions that started on head and trunk then progressed to peripheries. On examination, he was febrile with skin lesions appearing as crops of papules, vesicles with surrounding erythema. The mother gave a history of a similar incident happening last week in his school. The parents are worried since there is an immunodeficient child at home. What would be the best action plan to protect the immunodeficient kid?

options.text: It is a self-limiting disease with no risk
Oral antiviral therapy for the immunodeficient child
Specific immunoglobulin for the immunodeficient child

questions.stem: Which of the following represents a fetal complication from maternal infection with Parvovirus B19?

options.text: May lead to fetal hydrops and death
Severe fetal skin disease with eye involvement

questions.stem: During counseling an HIV positive mother who is pregnant and had several concerns regarding the outcome of her pregnancy. Her viral load is detectable although she is on treatment. What would be the best advice during counseling the mother?

options.text: The neonate should not receive any therapy after delivery
She can breastfeed normally if she continued on the therapy
She should deliver by cesarean section to decrease the chance of transmission
Therapy during pregnancy will not prevent the transmission of the virus to the baby

questions.stem: An 8-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Clinic with weakness, headache, nausea and anorexia that began 1 week before. Physical examination shows pitting edema, grade 2+ on the edema scale, over the eyelids and ankles. There is pallor of the skin, mucous membranes and nail beds. A 24-hour urine collection reveals a urine production of 20 ml per hour while the boy's bodyweight is 27 kg. The urine appears Dark brown. Blood pressure 140/100 mm Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 36 /min Temperature 38.6° C What clinical history would be most important for the diagnosis?
Children with septic shock need to be rapidly stabilized and resuscitated for their life saving. Which of the following has lowest evidence of benefit in their management?

During normal newborn exam, an absent red reflex in the eye and cardiac mummer are discovered. After interviewing the mother, she gave a history of viral infection during the first trimester. Which of the following infection can cause this?
In colonized mother with Group B Streptococcal infections, which of the following is risk factor for infection in the newborn?

A 6-years-old boy who has been treated since infancy for eczema is coming now to be evaluated for honey-colored crusted lesion in antecubital skin area bilaterally. He has no fever but skin infection is suspected. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the skin infection?

A 6-year-old boy who has been treated since infancy for eczema is coming now to be evaluated for severely itching umbilicated vesico-pustular skin rash that is grouped in "clusters of grapes* appearance overlying diffuse eczematous plaques. A superimposed skin infection is suspected. Which of the following is the most likely etiology?

A full term boy was born to a mother diagnosed antenatally with hepatitis B surface Ag positive (HBAg positive). Her delivery was unremarkable and the newborn weighed 3.4 kg and was normal on assessment. He received the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulins within the first 4 hours. The mother is very enthusiastic to breastfeed her child as she did with her previous children. Which of the following is the best advice?

A full term girl was born to a mother who is hepatitis B surface Ag positive (HbAg +ve). The baby weighs 3.2 kg and is asymptomatic. What is the appropriate immunoprophylaxis that should be considered in the first 12 hours?

options.text: Give hepatitis B vaccine and immunoglobulins
Measure hepatitis B surface antigen in the newborn

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child of a parent who was recently diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis has a tuberculin skin test. After 72 hours, the size of local induration is 10 mm. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?

A 2-year-old child presents to the clinic with chalky discoloration on both sides of the teeth. The child sleeps with the milk bottle in his mouth. On examination, there are opaque discolorations on the backsides of the central maxillary incisors and the first molars. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department with fever, headache and generalized muscular pain over the last 24 hours. The child appears sleepy and irritable. There are several spots on the buttocks and legs. Physical examination confirms stiffness of the neck. After performing a lumbar puncture, an intravenous infusion of penicillin G is started (see image, lab result and report). Blood pressure 90/55 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 38 /min Temperature 39° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Test Result (Normal Value) WBC 25 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) CSF Culture: Gram negative diplococci. Which of the following is the most likely late complication?

A 3-year-old boy presents to the Pediatric Emergency Department with fever, headache and generalized muscular pain over the last 24 hours. The child appears sleepy and irritable. There are several spots on the buttocks and legs. Physical examination confirms stiffness of the neck. After performing a lumbar puncture, an intravenous infusion of penicillin G is started. The parents also report that the child's 6-year-old brother had been in close contact with this boy and ask how best to look after him (see image and report). Blood pressure 90/55 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 38 /min Temperature 39° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air CSF analysis: Elevated cell count and Gram negative diplococci. What would be the best management for the older brother?

A 3-year-old girl presents with a high-grade fever and chills. Physical examination confirms that she is anemic with splenomegaly. Clinical Image with giemsa stain is shown (see image). Which of the following is the most likely etiology?

A 5-year-old boy presents with a sore throat and refusal to eat. The mother reported that the child has had an increased temperature for the last 3 days. Several children that attended the same play group have developed similar symptoms. Physical examination shows spots and blisters on the palm of both hands as well as on the buttocks. There are small ulcers on the palate (see image). Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 38.6° C Which of the following additional physical findings is most likely to have?

A 10-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Clinic with a skin rash. The parents report that the symptoms had started with a single red spot over a small scratch and have spread over the 4 days. There are several lesions on the cheeks, the trunk and the upper limbs. Physical examination confirms swollen lymph nodes in the armpits and groins (see image). Blood pressure 100/65 mg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 37.4° C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 10-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Clinic with a skin rash. The parents report that the symptoms had started with a single red spot over a small scratch and have spread over the 4 days. There are several lesions on the cheeks, the trunk and the upper limbs. Physical examination confirms swollen lymph nodes in the armpits and groins (see image). Blood pressure 100/65 mg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 37.4° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old girl presents with ear pain and swelling of the pinna. She had returned the previous day from the swimming camp and developed these complaints 1 day before. On examination, she has significant pain when moving the pinna and a foul smelling discharge from the ear canal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 1-year-old girl presents to the Paediatrics Emergency Department at night with episodes of loud cough and refusal to feed. There is a history of upper airway infection with nasal congestion and sneezing over the last week. She has not received any routine immunizations. During the physical examination, there are repetitive violent fits of a hacking cough that are followed by forceful, high-pitched inhalations and accompanied by facial cyanosis. Between attacks the girl appeared exhausted and apathetic. Heart rate 150 /min Respiratory rate 60 /min Temperature 36.6° C Oxygen saturation 92% on room air Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 5-year-old childis brought to the clinic with a febrile illness with a cough and separate irregularly shaped (blotchy) rashes. He has not had any routine vaccinations. On physical examination, there are enlarged tender cervical lymph nodes. There are also erythematous maculopapular rashes behind the ear, face and neck and to a lesser extent on the trunk. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents with a low-grade fever, malaise, conjunctivitis, coryza, and a cough. Recently, a rash of discrete pink macules began on the face and extends to the hands and feet. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 6-month-old infant develops a cough, coryza, fever, expiratory wheezing, grunting, tachypnea, rib retractions, and air trapping. Which of the following is optimal immediate treatment?

A 6-year-old child presents with malaise, fever, cough, nasal discharge, and conjunctivitis. Several days later the patient develops a maculopapular rash starting on the face and rapidly spreading to the rest of the body. Which of the following viruses is most likely the cause?

A 3-year-old child presents with a 1-week history of malaise, anorexia, nasal discharge, and conjunctivitis. The parent states that the child has also had 2 days of paroxysmal coughing spells with a stridor "whoop." Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 15-year-old child presents to the Outpatient Clinic suffering from abdominal pain, diarrhoea, and tenesmus for the last 2 weeks. There is mucus and blood present in the stool. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old has a 3-day history of fever, irritability, and anorexia. Examination confirms painful vesicles over the mucosa of the soft palate and posterior pharynx, sparing the gingiva and anterior oral cavity. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 39.0° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old child was prescribed antibiotics for treatment of a chest infection. 6 weeks after cessation of antibiotics, the patient presents with fever, abdominal pain, and profuse watery stools for the past month. Investigation confirms faecal leukocytes. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?

An 18-month-old child presents to the Emergency Department after a brief, generalised tonic clonic seizure. He has had a large, watery stool that had both blood and mucus in it. He is now postictal. Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 40.0° C Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 7-year-old child is brought to the Emergency Department with a history of fever and vomiting for 2 days. On examination, he is dehydrated, comatose and acidotic (see lab results). CSF Test Result (Normal Values) Cells 20 (0-3 / uL) Total Protein 0.45 (0.22-0.33 g/L) Glucose 3.5 (2.50-4.8 mmol/L) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child suddenly developed a high fever, chills, and vomiting. Examination shows nuchal rigidity and a positive Kernig's sign. Petechial lesions are noted on both extremities and over the abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old, severely ill child has been irritable and pyrexial for 2 days. the child started vomiting. appeared drowsy, and has deteriorated rapidly during the day. In addition, a petechial rash started today which has spread extremely quickly around the body. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following organs is most commonly affected by mumps in a 4-year-old boy?

A child is brought to Paediatric Clinic with cough, fever, rhinorrhoea, malaise, with conjunctival erythema. There are small, greyish, irregular lesions surrounded by an erythematous base, on the buccal mucous membrane near the second molar teeth. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A previously healthy 13-month-old girl comes to the clinic with a 2-day history of fever and increasing cough. She continued to be breastfed with no vomiting. Her immunizations are up to date. She is alert and mildly ill-appearing. On examination, there is no grunting or chest retraction. She has crackles heard over the right lung base. The remainder of the examination findings is normal. Bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is suspected. ● Respiratory rate: 36 /min ● Temperature: 38.6 °C ● Oxygen saturation: 96 % Which of the following would indicate a need for hospitalization?

options.text: Respiratory rate of 36 breath per min
Inability to maintain hydration or oral intake

questions.stem: A 6-month-old infant with cough and fever diagnosed as bronchiolitis. On examination, she had mild distress with intercostal retraction and chest auscultation reveals diffuse crackles. Blood pressure 92/67 mmHg Heart rate 145 /min Respiratory rate 56 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 89 % Which of the following is the best management?

options.text: Admit for oxygen and hydration therapy
Send home with instruction when to come back
Admit for antibiotics and oxygen administration
Admit for bronchodilation and steroid management

questions.stem: Which of the following asthmatic patients require hospital admission?

options.text: Oxygen saturation below 92% after high dose therapy

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child presented with recurrent chest infection and poor growth. On examination, chest auscultation revealed inspiratory crepitation with expiratory wheeze and finger clubbing. Further exploration in the history revealed the presence of very offensive and greasy stools. Which of the following is expected to be further identified in the physical examination?

A 3-year-old child presented to Emergency Room with fever, headache and lethargy. On examination, clear purpuric rash, sign of shock and positive Kernig sign present. Eye exam revealed the presence of papilledema. The parents are bedside and worried about child condition and prognosis. Which of the following complication is important for the parents?

A 3-year-old child presented to Emergency Room with difficulty breathing, lip swelling and spreading skin rash. On examination, marked airway swelling was observed with rash covering all the body. The mother said he was attending a party at his friend's house and she was not with him. Which of the following will likely reveal the diagnosis?

A 3-month-old girl presented to the Emergency Room with symptoms of paroxysmal episodes of cough followed by a whooping sound at the end. It is occasionally associated with perioral cyanosis and post- tussive vomiting. These symptoms got worse when she started to have a fever of 39.5°C. History revealed she did not receive her 2-month vaccine. Which of the following is the most common expected complication?

A 3-month-old girl presented to the Emergency Room with symptoms of paroxysmal episodes of cough followed by a whooping sound at the end. It is occasionally associated with perioral cyanosis and post- tussive vomiting. These symptoms got worse when she started to have a fever of 39.5°C. History revealed she did not receive her 2-month vaccine. What is the gold standard method to diagnose this condition?

A 3-month-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with history of paroxysmal episodes of staccato cough, inspiration between each cough. It is associated with perioral cyanosis and post-tussive vomiting. There is no history of diarrhea. This illness has been preceded by conjunctivitis few days ago. On examination, the child looks unwell and tachypneic with auscultatory crackles. He has normal white blood cell count with elevated eosinophils on laboratory evaluation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with history of paroxysmal episodes of cough associated with an inspiratory whoop and possessive emesis. It is associated with fever, conjunctival redness and diarrhoea. His immunization is up to date. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with history of paroxysmal episodes of staccato cough, inspiration between each cough. It is associated with perioral cyanosis and post-tussive vomiting. This illness was preceded by conjunctivitis a few days ago. On examination, the child looks unwell and tachypneic with crackles. Laboratory evaluation shows normal white blood cell count with elevated eosinophils. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-minute-old preterm infant at 27 weeks presents with tachypnea, labored breathing and chest wall recession. Blood pressure 55/135 mmHg Heart rate 135 /min Respiratory rate 65 /min Temperature 36.2 °C Oxygen saturation 86%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A term baby delivered by cesarean section, started to be tachypnic with nasal flaring and expiratory grunting. Chest X-ray showed fluid in the horizontal fissure Blood pressure 60/35 mmHg Heart rate 140 /min Respiratory rate 65 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 92 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-hour-old newborn delivered by cesarean section because of severe fetal deceleration and meconium stained fluid. He required intubation and ventilation with iontropic support. Few hours later, he started to have low saturation with increase oxygen requirement. The pre ducal saturation is 92 while the post ductal saturation is 81. Chest X-ray done and showed no pneumothorax. Which of the following is the next step in the management?

A term infant delivered with antenatal diagnosis of diaphragmatic hernia. She required vigorous resuscitation in the delivery room. Which of the following is the first step in managing this infant after stabilization?

A 6-month-old infant presents to the Emergency Room with sudden apnea and color change. The mother gave history of recurrent vomiting, and multiple chest infections. On examination, he looks failing to thrive with dystonic neck posturing while crying. Which of the following is considered a high-risk case for the above disease?

A 5-year-old child presents with a severe sore throat, high fever and increasing difficulty breathing over 8 hours. On examination, ill and toxic looking child with drooling of saliva and sitting immobile with an open mouth. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 38.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 2-month-old infant presents to Emergency Room with bronchiolitis required non-invasive mechanical ventilation as a respiratory support. Which of the following is the most appropriate destination?

options.text: Admission to pediatrics critical care unit

questions.stem: An 8-month-old infant admitted to Pediatrics Critical Care for close observation. Which of the following standers continuous monitoring in pediatrics critical care measured as trans-cutaneous?
Which of the following measures would decrease the incidence of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome?

A 20-month-old child is brought to the Emergency Department due to respiratory distress with stridor and fever. Her parents mention that 2 days ago she started rhinorrhoea and mild cough with progressive worsening of the cough that is now "barky". Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-week-old baby is brought to the clinic with low-grade fever and difficulty breathing. Her parents report that she had 2 episodes in which she appeared to have stopped breathing. Physical examination confirms subcostal retractions with Inspiration and diffuse bilateral wheeze. Temperature 37.9 °C Heart Rate 130 /min Respiratory Rate 55 /min Oxygen saturation 90% Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 10-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital due to acute exacerbation of asthma. He is currently medicated with montelukast once daily and has last been seen by his primary care physician over 6 months ago. He reports daily episodes of dry cough and wheezing that are exacerbated by exercise. After admission, his symptoms stabilized with the administration of inhaled albuterol. Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term maintenance therapy?

options.text: Oral steroids once daily, plus a long-acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Inhaled corticosteroid twice-daily, plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Inhaled long-acting beta-2 agonist, plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Leukotriene receptor antagonist once daily plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed

questions.stem: A 5-week-old baby is brought to the clinic with low-grade fever and difficulty breathing. Her parents report that she had 2 episodes in which she appeared to have stopped breathing. Physical examination confirms subcostal retractions with inspiration and diffuse bilateral wheeze. Temperature 37 °C Heart rate 130 /min Which of the following is the most frequent agent causing acute bronchiolitis?

A 3-year-old child admitted to the hospital to initiate antibiotic treatment for pneumonia. She has long history of sinusitis and lower respiratory tract infections. During the current admission, she underwent fibre optic bronchoscopy with sputum collection and both pseudomonas aeruginosa and burkholderia cepacia are isolated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child is a known asthmatic who usually has 1 acute exacerbation each month. The acute symptoms are relieved by nebulizer therapy at the Emergency Department or the nearby health centre. Which of the following should be included in the daily management?

A 22-month-old boy presents to the Emergency Department with a sudden onset of respiratory distress during a family picnic. He is febrile and has otherwise been well. Physical examination demonstrates unilateral wheezing in the right hemithorax. Which of the following is the most likely to be seen in his chest X-ray?

options.text: Consolidation of the right lower lobe
Lower lobe collapse on the right side
Hyperinflation of the right lung with mediastinal shift\ to the left

questions.stem: A 2-month -old bay presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department with coughing, wheezing and rapid breathing for the last 2 days. The infant was bom at 38 weeks' gestation; his birth weight is 3.5 kg and now weighs 5.2 kg. He had developed a runny nose, imitability and difficulties feeding without having to pause several times. His 3-year-old brother has a cold with fever and cough. Physical examination shows a prolonged expiratory time, nasal flaring and subcostal retractions. Cardiac auscultation results are normal and the spleen and liver are of normal size for the child's age. Blood pressure 86/58 mmHg Heart rate 146 /min Respiratory rate 56 /min Temperature 38.6° C Oxygen saturation 96% on room air Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in making a definitive diagnosis?

A 1-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a high fever, cough and respiratory distress for 3 days. On auscultation of the chest, there are generalised fine crackles (see report). Chest X-ray: Showed puffy infiltrates with ill-defined margins throughout both lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old sickle cell child arrives at the Emergency Department in respiratory distress. Over the previous 3 days, the child has become progressively tired and pale (see lab result). Hb 31 112-165 g/L Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 3-year-old alert and oriented giri presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department at 2 a.m. with breathing difficulties and a brassy, barking cough. There is inspiratory stridor at rest and a hoarse voice. The giri has been suffering from a viral upper airway infection for the past week. A physical examination shows moderate chest wall retractions. On auscultation, there is decreased air entry. The extremities and buccal membranes appear pink and moist. Heart rate 180 /min Respiratory rate 60 /min Temperature 39.9* C rectal Oxygen saturation 93% on room air Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 7-month-old presents with low-grade fever and a dry cough for the last 3 days. On examination, there is wheezing over both lung fields (see report). Heart Rate 127 /min Respiratory Rate 47 /min Temperature 38.9° C Chest X-ray: Hyperinflation and some infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old is brought to the clinic with sore throat and high-grade fever for 5 days. On examination, he is febrile and mildly dehydrated. The pharynx and tonsillar area is congested along with inflammation of the mouth and lips associated with gingivitis. Lesions in the mouth and lips appear as whitish-yellow plaques with erythematous base. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A16-year-old asymptomatic boy presents for a sports participation physical examination. He is asthmatic since the age of 4 years and uses albuterol on rare occasion, which gives rapid and complete relief. Which of the following questions is best to ask to evaluate whether the current control is satisfactory?

options.text: "Are you able to keep up with your teammates?"
"Are you using your inhaler more frequently?"

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl with presents with a sore throat and a temperature of 38°C. History reveals, she has not received any childhood immunisation. A clinical examination confirms a severely swollen and edematous neck region with enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Her pharynx is erythematous with bleeding spots when a swab is taken for culture. An inspiratory stridor is noted upon auscultation of the lungs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month old child is brought to the clinic with mild atopic eczema. The parents report that he woke up last night with stridor and a barking cough. There are no preceding or associated upper respiratory tract infection symptoms. The symptoms resolved spontaneously a few hours later. It is the second episode of this nature over the past 6 months. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis ?

A 1-year-old girl is brought to the Paediatric Emergency Department in the early morning with breathing difficulties. She has a dry cough that sounds like the barking of a sea lion and gets worse when she is crying. Every time the infant breathes in, there is a high-pitched sound. There is also a 4-day history of a mild upper airway infection. Blood pressure 80/65 mmg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 40 /min Temperature 38.5° C Which of the following is the most appropriate way to establish the diagnosis?

A 6-month-old boy presents to the paediatrician with a loud barking cough and a rectal temperature of 38° C. The parents report a cold for the last 3 days that worsens at night. The coughing is aggravated with crying and there is a high-pitched, rasping sound on inhalation. Physical examination confirms a reddened throat and a nasal obstruction (see report). Chest X-ray: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department at night with a barking, dry cough and laboured breathing. There is a 3-day history of nasal obstruction and cough that had worsened over the last 2 hours. The child appears anxious and cries with a hoarse voice. There is a sharp, high-pitched sound on inspiration. Physical examination confirms indrawing of the chest wail and a reddened throat. A single treatment with nebulized epinephrine results.in a quick improvement of the airway symptoms. 30 minutes after the inhalation the coughing and the breathing difficulties reappear. Which of the following is the next step in management?

An 8-month-old child presents to the Pediatric Emergency Department in the early morning hours. He has laboured breathing and a barking cough that becomes worse when crying. There is a 2-day history of nasal congestion and dry cough. Physical examination confirms nasal flaring and a reddened throat. There is also a harsh, high-pitched sound when the child breathes in. Auscultation over the lung fields is normal. The boy is anxious and cries with a hoarse voice. Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 39° C Oxygen saturation 94% on room air Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 12-month-old boy presents to the Pediatric Emergency Department in the early morning hours with nasal congestion and a barking cough and 3 days history of a mild airway infection. Physical examination shows suprasternal retractions and nasal flaring. The back of the throat is reddened. Lung fields are clear on auscultation. The inhalation of nebulized epinephrine temporarily improves the symptoms. Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 38.5° C Oxygen saturation 94% on room air Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 4-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department at 3 a.m. with a barking cough and mild respiratory distress. The parents report that he had an airway infection over the last 2 days that had suddenly worsened. The boy appears irritable. Physical examination confirms an inspiratory stridor. The child speaks with a hoarse voice. Blood pressure 90/65 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 38° C Oxygen saturation 92% on room air Which additional finding would be cause for concern?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department in the early morning hours with a barking cough that worsens with crying. There is a history of mild cough and temperatures around 38° C (rectal) over the last 3 days. Physical examination confirms an inflamed throat and mild suprasternal retractions. Blood pressure 95/65 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 34 /min Temperature 39.3° C Which of the following is the most likely at auscultatory finding?

A 4-year-old girl presents with morning limp and swelling of her right knee that has been worsening for the last 2 months. On physical examination, she clearly has decreased range of motion as well as swelling and warmth of the right knee. She has negative antinuclear antibody (ANA). When should she be screened for uveitis by an ophthalmologist?

options.text: Not recommended if her ANA is negative

questions.stem: A 4-year-old girl presents with morning limp and swelling of her both knees that has been worsening for the last 2 months. She has no other symptoms. On physical examination, she clearly has decreased range of motion as well as swelling and warmth of both knees. She has normal laboratory investigation except a positive antinuclear antibody (ANA). Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) suspected. Which of the following is the best classification of her disease?

A 6-year-old girl presents to the clinic complaining of morning neck stiffness and pain in her finger joints to the degree that she needs help in buttoning herself. She has flat erythema over the malar eminences that are sparing the nasolabial folds. One examination, she had painless mouth ulcer. On her finger's joints, there is clear swelling and tenderness. Which of the following will make her fulfill 4 of the 11 American College of Rheumatology criteria for the classification of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus?
A 2.5-year-old boy seen in the clinic with skin rash. There is history of mild abdominal pain but the child looks healthy otherwise (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy presented to the Emergency Room for the second time with non-resolving high- grade fever (39.5 °C). Fever started 6 days ago and was prescribed antipyretic, which did not help much in relieving the fever. Instead, He has developed bilateral non-exudative conjunctivitis. His immunizations are up-to-date. On examination, he has diffusely erythematous oropharynx, red cracked lips, and a strawberry tongue. He has non-exudative congested throat with cervical lymph node that measure around 1.5 cm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy presented to the Emergency Room for the second time with non-resolving high- grade fever (39.5 °C). Fever started 6 days ago and was prescribed antipyretic, which did not help much in relieving the fever. Instead, He has developed bilateral non-exudative conjunctivitis. His immunizations are up-to-date. On examination, he has diffusely erythematous oropharynx, red cracked lips, and a strawberry tongue. He has non-exudative congested throat with a cervical lymph node that measures around 1.5 cm. IVIG is ordered. Which of the following may indicate a poor response to IVIG in such a patient?

A 4-year-old boy is diagnosed with Kawasaki Disease on day 8 of illness. He is admitted to the hospital for further management. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment regimen?

A 4-year-old boy is diagnosed with Kawasaki Disease on day 6 of illness. He is admitted to the hospital for further management. He has received aspirin and IVIG without any complications. His fever has subsided and his conjunctivitis has significantly improved. Which of the following modalities is the best to evaluate his coronary arteries?

An 8-year-old girl is brought to the Paediatric Clinic with pain in the left wrist and right knee. These symptoms have occurred several times in the past 6 months with asymptomatic periods in between. Usually, the pain is worse in the morning and it improves during the day. She is otherwise healthy. On physical examination, there is swelling and a decreased range of motion of both joints. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-hour-old neonate found to have abnormal heart rhythm during admission exam. ECG done showed complete heart block. ECHO showed small persistent ductus arteriosus (see lab results). RBC 5 4.8-7.1 x 1012/L (Newborn) 4.6-4.8 x 1012/L (Child) Hb 165 165-195 g/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) HCT 0.45 0.44-0.64 (Newborn) 0.32-0.42 (Child) Platelets count 65 150-400 x 109/L WBC 11 9.1-30.1 x 109/L (Birth) 6.1-17.5 x 109/L (1-23 months) Which of the following maternal disorders contributes to the finding?
Which of the following is the main treatment of Kawasaki disease?

A 12-year-old girl presents with redness, frequent ptosis and diplopia. She has no myalgia or fasciculation and her deep tendon reflexes are 1-2+. She reports that the symptoms become worse as the day progresses and that she feels better in the morning. Which of the following is the most likely pathophysiology?

A healthy 3-month-old uncircumcised boy brought to the clinic by his parents with a history of fever since morning. He has not had nasal congestion, cough, or diarrhea. He had 1 episode of emesis when he was given acetaminophen. He has continued to breastfeed and has had a normal number of wet diapers. He is mildly ill-appearing. There is no discernible focus of infection on examination. Temperature 38.4 °C Which of the following factors is most strongly associated with an increased probability of having a urinary tract infection?

A 4-month-old uncircumcised boy brought to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of fever. He has not had vomiting, diarrhea, cough, or nasal congestion. There has been no known contact with ill persons. He has continued to breastfeed and has not had a decrease in the number of wet diapers. He is mildly ill-appearing but alert and interactive. Examination shows no focus of infection. A bag urine sample is collected and sent for urinalysis (see lab results). ● Temperature 39.1 °C ● Color: light yellow clear or light yellow ● pH: 8 (4.3-8) ● Specific gravity: 1030 (1001-1030) ● Protein: Absent (Absent) ● Glucose: Absent (Absent) ● Ketones: Absent (Absent) ● Nitrite: Positive (Absent) ● Leukocytes: 11 (0-3 per high power field) Which of the following results of urinalysis would increase the probability of having a urinary tract infection?

A 3-month-old boy presented with a history of fever for the last 2 days. On examination, he is circumcised and has no focus of infection. A urine sample obtained by bladder catheterization is performed. He was started on oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. After being at home, his mother is called and states that he is back to his normal activity with no more fevers. The mother is advised to have him complete the 10-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (see report). ● Urine culture: Grows 80,000 colony-forming units (CFU) per milliliter of Escherichia coli that is susceptible to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: No further imaging or treatment is indicated
Antibiotic prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole until 2 years of age

questions.stem: Which of the following methods of collection of urine for culture is most sensitive and reliable for establishing the diagnosis of a urinary tract infection?
What would be the best treatment of an uncomplicated cystitis in a 5-year-old girl?

A newborn boy is brought to the Paediatrics clinic. Examination shows abdominal distension with palpable kidneys and a distended bladder (see report). Voiding cystourethrogram: Shows bilateral hydronephrosis and distension of the bladder and proximal urethra. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is not necessary to diagnose Nephrotic Syndrome?

A 5-year-old boy presented with eye puffiness and lower limb edema. He has no fever, vomiting or abdominal pain. His physical examination revealed well-perfused extremities and lower limb pitting edema. The rest of his exam is unremarkable. Color: Clear clear or light yellow pH: 6 4.3-8 Specific gravity: 1010 1001-1030 Protein: ++ Absent Glucose: Absent Absent Ketones: Absent Absent Nitrite: Absent Absent Hemoglobin: Absent Absent Leukocytes: 0 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes: 0 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in such a patient?

A 5-year-old boy presented with eye puffiness and lower limb edema. He has no fever, vomiting or abdominal pain. His physical examination revealed well-perfused extremities and lower limb pitting edema. The rest of his exam is unremarkable. His laboratory testing confirmed the diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome. After starting him on treatment, Which of the following defines complete remission?

options.text: Urine dipstick negative or trace reading for 3 consecutive days
Urine dipstick negative or trace reading for 5 consecutive days

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy presented with eye puffiness and lower limb edema. He has no fever, vomiting or abdominal pain. His physical examination revealed well-perfused extremities and lower limb pitting edema. The rest of his exam is unremarkable. His laboratory testing confirmed the diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome. He is started on steroid treatment. Which of the following is used to define steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome?

options.text: Inability to induce a remission within 4 weeks of daily steroid therapy
Inability to induce a remission within 4 months of daily steroid therapy
Inability to induce a remission within 12 days of daily steroid therapy
Inability to induce a remission within 12 weeks of daily steroid therapy

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy presents to the clinic with abdominal pain, malaise, fever, nausea and vomiting. He has a history of 2 urinary tract infections. A contrast voiding cysto-urethrogram is requested (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy presented with eye puffiness and lower limb edema. He has no fever, vomiting or abdominal pain. His physical examination revealed well-perfused extremities and lower limb pitting edema. The rest of his exam is unremarkable. His laboratory testing confirmed the diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome. Which of the following is the first line of treatment in this patient?

A 3-year-old child presents with a history of increasing eye puffiness for 1 week especially in the morning. He has had flu-like illness 2 week ago. On examination, he looks well, not in distress and no lower limb edema. Eye, chest and abdomen exams are normal (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18/min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Color Clear clear or light yellow Protein +4 Glucose Absent Leukocytes 0 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 0 Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 5-year-old child presents with a history of increasing eye puffiness for 1 week, especially in the morning. He has had flu-like illness 2 week ago. On examination, he looks well, not in distress and no lower limb edema. Eye, chest and abdomen exams are normal (see lab results). Blood pressure 100/70 mmHg Heart rate 88 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Total Proteins 35 56-80 g/L Albumin 16 36-52 g/L Protein +4 Absent Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents with history of increasing eye puffiness for 1 week especially in the morning. He has had flu-like illness 2 week ago. On examination, he looks well, not in distress and no lower limb edema. Eye, chest and abdomen exams are normal (see lab result). Total Cholesterol 3 <5.2 mmol/L Triglycerides 10 <1.7 mmol/L Protein +4 Absent Leukocytes 0 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 0 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 5-year-old child presents to the Emergency Room with vomiting and diarrhea for 4 days. On examination, he looks dehydrated, hypoactive with sunken eyes, doughy skin and dry mucous membrane. The capillary refill is 4 seconds. Blood pressure 90/70 mmH Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the expected serum sodium level based on clinical finding?

A 5-year-old child presents to the Emergency Room with vomiting and diarrhea for 4 days. On examination, he looks dehydrated, hypoactive with sunken eyes and delayed skin turger with dry mucous membrane and capillary refill is 4 seconds. The child connected to cardiopulmonary monitor and IV access attained, blood sample sent for electrolytes. Blood pressure 60/40 mmH Heart rate 134 /min Respiratory rate 23 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: 20 ml per kg normal saline bolus
Start maintenance fluid waiting for serum electrolytes

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child has asymptomatic hematuria. There is no significant past medical history and the physical examination is unremarkable (see lab result). Urinalysis Result Normal Value Erythrocytes 15 0-2 per HPF Which of the following should the initial evaluation include?

A 6-year-old boy complains of passing Coca cola-coloured urine for the last week. On examination, he had a congested throat, and anterior cervical lymphadenopathy (see lab results). Blood pressure 155/100 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 20/min Temperature 38.5° C Urinalysis Result Normal Values Colour Brown Clear or light yellow Appearance Turbid Clear Leukocytes 3-5 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 20-30 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old boy complains of passing tea-coloured urine for the last 3 days. On examination, there is a congested throat, with no other abnormal findings (see lab results). Blood pressure 140/98 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 20/min Temperature 37.5° C Urinalysis Result Normal Values Colour Brown tea Clear or light yellow Appearance Turbid Clear Leukocytes 3-5 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 20-30 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the Emergency Department with fever and dark urine. Her parents state that she had been constipated. On examination, she looks unwell and irritable with abdominal tenderness, but no palpable liver or spleen. Blood pressure 125/86 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 29 /min Temperature 39.9°C Test Result Normal Values WBC 16.5 4.5-10.5 x 10^9/L Hb 81 112-160 g/L Platelets count 325 150-400 x 10^9/L Urinalysis Test Result Normal Values Leukocytes 16 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 18 0-2 per high power field Protein ++ Absent Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the Emergency Department with fever and dark urine. Her parents state that she had been constipated. On examination, she looks unwell and irritable with abdominal tenderness, but no palpable liver or spleen (see lab results). Blood pressure 125/86 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 29/min Temperature 39.9° C Hb 81 112-160 g/L Platelets count 325 150-400 x 109/L Urinalysis Test Result Normal Values Leukocytes 16 0-3 per high power field I Erythrocytes 18 0-2 per high power field Protein ++ Absent Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old boy presents to the Outpatient Clinic with a 2-week history of facial swelling, poor dietary Intake and reduced activity with positive sacral edema (see lab results). Blood pressure 95/65 mmHg Heart rate 95 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 36.8° C Hb 94 112-160 g/L Alanine aminotransferase 52 10-35 U/L Albumin 25 36-52 g/L Total Cholesterol 7.0 <5.2 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
